title: Quant profile intake conductor and canary logbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable, auditable intake pipeline and canary logbook for quantization profiles (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) so that new precision artifacts can be validated, pinned, and published with an automatic regression signal that ties into model pinning and rollout policies.
context: We onboard dozens of low-precision variants every week. Current intake is manual and fraught: inconsistent metadata, missing perf traces, and late discovery of quality regressions during customer rollouts. That increases blast radius and manual ops for PM/QA/infra. We need a single conductor that standardizes artifacts, runs a deterministic canary battery, records canonical signatures (latency/quality/kv-cache behavior), and wires alerts into the rollout automation.
proposed_solution: Build a modular intake service (Quant Intake Conductor) that: 1) ingests uploaded quant artifacts and metadata; 2) normalizes profiles (kernel/quant params, hardware tags); 3) executes a canary battery covering perf microbenchmarks and a small eval suite; 4) records a 'logbook' artifact with metric signatures and failure reasons; 5) computes delta scores vs. pinned baseline and assigns a canary verdict (PASS / WARN / FAIL); 6) publishes metadata to the pin registry and signals rollout pipelines. Add a lightweight UI in Console for logbook inspection and a webhook for automated rollback when regressions exceed thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor accepts quant artifacts (tarball + manifest) and returns a unique artifact id
Canary battery runs automatically on a dedicated infra pool and produces reproducible metric set (latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, memory footprint, KV cache hit delta, task-quality deltas)
Logbook JSON is stored and indexed (artifact id -> signature) and is queryable from Console
Delta thresholds are applied and a canonical verdict (PASS/WARN/FAIL) is computed and persisted
Artifacts with FAIL verdict are blocked from automated rollout and create an incident ticket with failure details and links
PRD + tests added, and CI gate prevents publishing of artifacts without a logbook
tasks: Design artifact manifest schema (include quant backend, seed/hyperparams, calibration dataset hash)
Implement conductor ingest API and validation checks
Author canary battery (microbench + mini-eval harness) for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ
Instrument telemetry hooks to capture per-token timing and KV cache traces
Build logbook storage and indexer; add search fields for model, backend, hardware, verdict
Integrate with pin registry and rollout automation to respect verdicts
Expose minimal Console view for engineers and PMs to inspect logbook entries
Write end-to-end tests and CI gates; add a checklist for manual review exemptions
metrics: Canary coverage: percentage of incoming artifacts that run the full battery (target 95%)
False positive rate on PASS->FAIL transitions (target <3%)
Time-to-logbook: median end-to-end time from upload to verdict (target <30m)
Rollout aborts triggered by conductor (count/month; baseline 0)
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal-only for infra and research artifacts (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in publishing for trusted partners, add UI. Phase 3: enforce CI gate for all publications and enable automatic blocking when FAIL (target end of quarter). Each phase includes a one-week canary where only <1% of traffic is served by newly published artifacts.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing, e2e integration test that runs the canary battery on a simulated artifact, performance smoke tests for P95 latency budget, and a negative test set proving that known regressions are detected and marked FAIL. Add nightly synthetic sweep to detect drift in canary baselines.
notes: Novel additions compared to current intake: canonical logbook signatures (immutable), delta-scoring that is workload-aware (not just single-number latency), and explicit linkage to pin registry to prevent human error during rollouts. Will coordinate with Solutions and Console teams for UI affordances.
